source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Diagnose individual client infections directly, similar to what the staff member is currently assuming is the actual purpose of these environmental cultures","B":"Identify potential pathogen reservoirs and evaluate how well cleaning practices are actually working","C":"Serve no practical infection control purpose, contrary to why this kind of periodic environmental surveillance is actually performed","D":"Replace the need for standard cleaning protocols, which is not the actual purpose or effect of this particular surveillance practice"}}
source_row.rationale: Environmental culture surveillance helps identify potential reservoirs of pathogens on surfaces and evaluate the effectiveness of current cleaning and disinfection practices.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Environmental Surveillance in Healthcare Settings
source_row.stem: An infection prevention team periodically cultures environmental surfaces in an ICU, and a staff member assumes these cultures are really meant to diagnose individual clients' own infections directly rather than serve any broader purpose. This surveillance instead helps:
